rows.07:fc08:
I decided to search the first-floor boys' bathroom.
What a filthy bathroom, though.
The boys' bathroom had four urinals and two stalls.
...I didn't really want to search in here, but my life was on the line.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:fd20:
I shone the light on the row of four urinals.
Ugh...!
They were crawling with cockroaches.
The moment the light hit them, they all scattered at once.
I searched carefully, but it didn't seem to be here.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:fde0: I decided to check the stall at the back.{p}
rows.07:fe20:
...Surely it wouldn't be inside the toilet bowl itself.
I searched every inch.{p}
rows.07:fea8: I decided to search somewhere else.{p}
rows.07:fef8:
I decided to go to the third-floor bathrooms.
There was a boys' bathroom and a girls' bathroom.{p}Which one should I check?
rows.07:ff90:
The girls' bathroom had four stalls.
I remembered hearing a rumor that Hanako-san haunted the girls' bathroom in the old school building.
But right now, nothing could scare me.
Time was slipping away fast.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:1008c: I decided to search the stall at the very back.{p}
rows.07:100c4:
I shone the light.
Then I searched every inch of the back stall.
...Nothing.
No good.
I'd better search somewhere else.{p}
rows.07:10144: I decided to search the second stall from the back.{p}
rows.07:10180:
I shone the light.
Then I searched every inch of the second stall from the back.
...Nothing.
No good.
No, wait!
Something was sitting on the ledge of the stall's frame.
I shone my flashlight on it.{p}
rows.07:10244:
It was an ampule filled with a yellow liquid.
I found it!
That's it!
I finally found it!
I reached out for it.{p}
rows.07:102c0:
"Kyeeeeeeeee!"
A shrill scream suddenly rang out, and the next instant something slammed into my back.
"Aaagh!"
Something was stuck in my shoulder.
I pulled it out. It was a mechanical pencil.
"Die! Just die!"
Someone was strangling me.
The flashlight had slipped from my hand and rolled away, and its beam lit up my attacker's face.{p}
rows.07:10410:
It was Fukuzawa.
"Let go!"
I shoved Fukuzawa away.
But she wouldn't let go.
"Aaagh!"
A searing pain shot across my face.
Fukuzawa had clawed me with her sharp nails.
I covered my face without thinking.
Fukuzawa sank her teeth into my hand.
...Damn it!
I was just one step away!{p}What do I do?!
rows.07:10558: I read out the title of that report.{p}If I remember right, the title was...
rows.07:105a4: A Hundred Days Concerning Human Life and Death
rows.07:105c0: A Hundred-Day Period of Human Life and Death
rows.07:105d8: Trends of Human Life and Death over a Hundred-Day Period
rows.07:105f4: Hundred-Day Trends Concerning Human Life and Death
rows.07:10614: Trends Concerning Human Life and Death over a Hundred-Day Period
rows.07:106dc:
"How do you know that★"
It was too dark to read, but I thrust the report in my hand out in front of Fukuzawa.
"I found this in the chemistry lab! You're a horrible girl.
Though any teacher who'd accept something like this is just as bad."
"Give it back!"
Fukuzawa tried to snatch the report away.
But I wasn't going to hand it over that easily.
"Whoa there! Is this so important to you?!"
I slipped out of Fukuzawa's grasp and held the report up high.
"Give it back to me!"
That report must have meant the world to Fukuzawa.
Of course it did.
It was an outrageous report that set out to record a human being's life right up until the moment of death.
"Ah!"
Fukuzawa clawed me, and the report fell from my hand.
Caught by the wind, the report fluttered up and flew out the window.{p}
rows.07:109dc:
Just as Fukuzawa reached out the window, the window frame snapped.
The wood of the frame had rotted through.
Along with dozens of pure white sheets of paper, Fukuzawa's body flew out into the air.
Even as she fell, Fukuzawa glared up at me, spitting out some kind of curse.
A sickening thud rang out, the sound of something heavy smashing into the ground, and I leaned out the window.
Carefully, so I wouldn't fall...{p}
rows.07:10b44:
Below, Fukuzawa lay spread-eagled on the ground.
Her neck was twisted at an impossible angle.
It was broken clean through.
In the moonlight, the report pages fluttered down onto her white sailor uniform like confetti.
The report chronicling life and death, never to be finished, kept piling up on top of Fukuzawa.
Perhaps Fukuzawa had completed her report with her own death.
...That's right.
I couldn't just stand around like this.{p}
rows.07:10e20:
I took deep breath after deep breath, then checked my watch again.
The appointed time had already passed.
...I was alive.
I was saved!
Tears spilled down my cheeks on their own.
So this was how wonderful it was to be alive.
For the first time in my life, I savored the joy of being alive.
...Thank God.
I let out another sigh.{p}What should I do?
Wait here until morning?
Or go home?
rows.07:10fb0:
Once I knew I was saved, the fear suddenly came flooding back stronger than before.
This was the old school building, in the dead of night.
I was far too frightened to wait in a place like this until morning.
I picked up the flashlight that had been knocked out of my hand and stood up.
Then, without really thinking, my eyes fell on the broken window frame.
Rotten, crumbling wood.
But it still seemed fairly sturdy.
An idea came to me.
...This might come in handy.
I picked up the broken piece of window frame.
Perhaps that was nothing less than a warning from God.{p}
rows.07:1117c:
...I felt dizzy.
Exhaustion crashed down on me all at once.
Still, I couldn't believe how much I'd managed to do.
I was impressed by my own stamina.
Staggering, I slowly put one leaden leg in front of the other.{p}
rows.07:11240:
Going down the stairs was agony.
With every step, I felt like my foot was about to slip.
There was no strength left in my legs at all.
By the time I finally made it down to the first floor, the sky was about to start turning pale.{p}
rows.07:1138c:
...And then.
There he stood, in front of the school gate.
Arms folded, he seemed to have been lying in wait for me.
"...Hino."
"You've really put up a fight, {a}.
I've played this human-hunting game plenty of times, but this is a first.
What do you say? Why don't you run the Murder Club with me?"
Hino smiled, his face perfectly pleasant.{p}
rows.07:114b8:
"..........Don't be stupid. I'd sooner die."
"...I see. That's a shame.
I thought you'd make a good partner.
I've disposed of everyone who betrayed us.
Kazama, Shindo, Hosoda too. There's no one left.
And I'm graduating soon.
I thought you could take over after me and make a fine club president.
Well? Won't you reconsider?"
"No way."
"So stubborn. Well, it can't be helped. Then I'll give up on you.
The Murder Club ends with me."{p}
rows.07:11668:
As we talked, I moved step by step toward the school gate where Hino was waiting.
"Hino. There's one thing I want to ask you."
"What is it?"
"What is a Murder Club even for?"
"I'm so glad you asked.
You see, people build up this thing called stress. But the elite must never let stress build up.
So what do you do about it?
That's right. You eliminate anything that might cause you stress.
You kill every last person who makes you angry.
That way, stress never builds up, and whatever stress you have just naturally melts away.
It's fun. Is there any other method as wonderful as this?"
"You're out of your mind."
"...Thank you. I'll take that as a compliment.
In every age, ordinary people never understand what a genius thinks.
Now, let's bring this to an end."{p}
rows.07:1191c:
Hino pulled out a knife.
I probably didn't even have the strength left to dodge.
Without a word, I thrust my hand into my pocket.
In my pocket was...{p}
rows.07:11a84:
Then Hino charged at me, swinging the knife.
There was only one path left to me...{p}What do I do?
rows.07:11afc: Deliberately let Hino stab me with his knife
rows.07:11b1c: Take out the screwdriver in my pocket
rows.07:11b48: Say I'll join the Murder Club
rows.07:11b60:
"Come on, Hino! Don't miss! Drive that knife into my gut as hard as you can!"
I shouted.
"Heh, giving up, are you?!"
Hino charged at me, laughing.
I focused every nerve I had on Hino's knife.
This was my last gamble.
If my luck held, it was sure to work.
It mustn't miss.
I had to take Hino's knife in exactly the right spot.{p}
rows.07:11ca8:
If it missed... I'd die!
"Let me put you out of your misery!"{p}
rows.07:11cd8:
"Ngh!"
A dull pain throbbed through my stomach.{p}
rows.07:11d1c:
The next moment, a look of dismay spread across Hino's face.
For Hino, this was something that should never have happened.
"You bastard... You tricked me."
"What's wrong, Hino? You've gone deathly pale."
With my left hand, I gripped Hino's hand, knife and all, where it was thrust into my stomach.
And with my right, I fumbled the screwdriver out of my pocket.{p}There wasn't a moment to lose.
What do I do?
rows.07:11e58: Drive the screwdriver into Hino's throat
rows.07:11e78: Drive the screwdriver into Hino's heart
rows.07:11e9c: Drive the screwdriver into Hino's shoulder
rows.07:11ec8: Without hesitating, I drove the screwdriver into Hino's shoulder.{p}
rows.07:11f14:
"Gyaah!"
Hino went tumbling to the ground.{p}
rows.07:11f44:
Hino's knife was still sticking out of my stomach.
I pulled the knife out.
...There wasn't a single drop of blood on it.
Because I had hidden the broken window frame from the old school building's bathroom inside my dress shirt. The screwdriver was buried in Hino's shoulder.
He was clutching his stabbed shoulder, shielding it.
Blood was faintly seeping through.{p}
